summary: Yakima County, WA lookout site on Yakama Nation land: a 1935 wooden tower fell, a 68-ft steel tower replaced it in 1937; now gone, access by permission only.

facts.design: 3-legged wooden tower (1935), replaced in 1937 by a 68-foot steel tower with a house at the bottom
facts.status_note: FFLOS and Firelookout.com list the tower as gone; Rex's page says removed; no source describes what remains on the site today

access.note: Yakama Nation land per WillhiteWeb, which says access is forbidden without special permission

facts.agency: Yakima Indian Reservation (administered by, per FFLOS); WillhiteWeb calls the land Yakama Nation

events.note: 3-legged wooden tower that fell down in its first year
68-foot steel tower with a house at the bottom for living quarters
Homer Lackey spent the summer on the lookout, which stood near the Vernon Parrish headquarters; Parrish employed him
Registered July 20, 2012 as FFLOS US 1367, WA 267; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built in 1935 as a 3-legged wooden tower that fell down the first year

evidence.supports: replaced in 1937 with a 68-foot steel tower and house, now gone
evidence.quote: That was replaced in 1937 with a 68' steel tower and house, which are now gone.

evidence.supports: the 1937 steel tower had a house at the bottom for living quarters
evidence.quote: So in 1937, a 68 foot steel tower was built with a house at the bottom for living quarters.

Rex's page marks the site as removed
summer 1938 lookout job near Vernon Parrish headquarters; Parrish is the one employing him

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS names the administrator as the Yakima Indian Reservation; WillhiteWeb calls the same land the Yakama Nation. The story uses the register's wording for the reservation and WillhiteWeb's wording for access.

notes_for_editor: Four short pages, several of them repeating one another; no photos, NRHP record or current visit report found. The staffing item rests on one July 1938 Goldendale Sentinel quote reprinted on Rex's page. Height 20.7 m converts the 68-ft 1937 tower, not the 1935 tower. The 1938 employer wording follows the source ('who is employing him'). No source describes the site today.
